components.name: Button
components.summary: Triggers actions and decisions. Six styles, two sizes, optional leading and trailing icon. Icon Button is a separate 44 by 44 component for icon-only actions.
whenToUse: Primary: the main action on the screen.
Secondary: alternative actions.
Ghost: lower visual weight.
Accent: emphasis.
Inverse: on dark backgrounds.
Destructive: irreversible or dangerous actions, such as delete or cancel.
whenNotToUse: Navigation to another page or section: use Link.

properties.name: Size
properties.note: Small exists only for Ghost in the current Figma set (4 of 28 variants).

contrastText.case: Inverse Default (text on its own fill)

accessibility.targetSize: Medium is 45 high and Icon Button is 44 by 44, which meets 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced, AAA). Small is 37 high, which meets 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum, AA, 24 by 24) but not 2.5.5.
accessibility.focus: In Figma the ring is a separate layer: no fill, 2px inside stroke bound to Border/Utilities/Focus Ring and Stroke/focus, with a 2px transparent gap (Stroke/focus-gap); square where the component radius is 0. In code it is an outline of 2px (--focus-ring-width) with a 2px offset (--focus-ring-gap) on every style.
accessibility.naming: Icon Button has no visible text. In code it needs an accessible name (aria-label), as the Figma description states.
accessibility.disabled: Disabled uses the disabled tokens, not opacity.

knownGaps.text: The Figma Info panel cites WCAG 2.4.7 and 2.4.12 for the focus ring. 2.4.12 is Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced, AAA). Ring appearance falls under 2.4.7 (AA) and 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (AAA). Source: TetraLogical, What's new in WCAG 2.2.
The description says sizes Medium and Small, but Small exists only for Ghost.
Accent Default fill is Background/Brand/Default in Figma Core, which matches the code (--color-bg-brand-default). Confirmed on 2026-11-20.
Destructive Default and Focus bind the primitive Functional/error, not a semantic Danger token. Hover binds the semantic Background/Danger/Hover.
Inverse in Light is a white fill with no border. On the default white page it is not visible. It is meant for dark surfaces.

unverified: Whether stroke weights are bound to Stroke variables (the check used a field key that may not apply).

components.name: Badge
components.summary: Compact, non-interactive label for themes, status and highlights. Brand styles (Ancora, Solar), semantic styles (Success, Danger) and Neutral.
whenToUse: Ancora: technical categories.
Solar: highlights and milestones.
Success: positive status.
Neutral: discreet labels, including content under construction (Draft was removed on 2026-11-20).
Danger: error or urgency states.
whenNotToUse: Anything interactive: use a Tag.

all.text: Body/Medium/body-sm medium, Plus Jakarta Sans Medium, 13, original case

Success.fill: Background/Positive/Secondary (12% in Light, solid in Dark)

Danger.fill: Background/Danger/Secondary (10% in Light, solid in Dark)

accessibility.note: All five styles meet 4.5:1 in both modes on the default page background. The tightest is Solar in Light (4.78). Badges on other surfaces must be re-measured.
accessibility.meaning: Colour alone must not carry the meaning: the label text states the status.

components.name: Link
components.summary: Text link for navigation and low emphasis actions. Two sizes and four states. Distinguished from surrounding text by underline.
whenToUse: Navigation to another page, section or resource.
Low emphasis actions.
whenNotToUse: The primary action of a screen: use Button.
Triggering actions that change data: use Button.

Hover.note: bold (700) instead of regular (400), same colour; the text is about 1px wider

Focus.note: bold like Hover, plus a square focus ring: 2px (Stroke/focus), 2px gap (Stroke/focus-gap), Border/Utilities/Focus Ring

accessibility.distinguishable: The link colour is the body text colour, so the underline is what separates a link from plain text.
accessibility.targetSize: Medium is 21 high and Small is 18 high, below the 24 by 24 of 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum, AA). Inline links inside a sentence are covered by the inline exception. Stand-alone links need spacing to meet it.
accessibility.naming: Every link needs a clear destination in its own text.

knownGaps.text: Hover and Focus switch from regular to bold, which widens the text by about 1px (Medium 25 to 26, Small 21 to 22), so neighbouring content shifts slightly. Accepted by the owner (D-32).
Stand-alone Small links (18 high) depend on surrounding spacing to meet 2.5.8.

components.name: Separator
components.summary: Decorative horizontal rule that separates blocks of content. One variant, no states, no navigation function.
whenToUse: Dividing groups of content inside a card, list or section when spacing alone is not enough.
whenNotToUse: Structure that assistive technology must announce: use headings and landmarks.
A vertical divider: Figma has no vertical variant.

all.width: 100 in the Figma specimen, full container width in CSS

accessibility.meaning: The line is decorative and carries no meaning, so it is hidden from assistive technology: <hr class="separator" aria-hidden="true">. It is exempt from the 3:1 non-text contrast of 1.4.11 because nothing depends on seeing it.
accessibility.specimenNote: The Figma specimen is 100 wide only to show the line. The CSS line fills its container.

components.name: Table
components.summary: Data table for comparing records across a few columns. A bordered wrapper with an optional caption, header cells, row headers and data cells. No sorting, selection, row hover or sticky header in this version.
whenToUse: Comparing several records across the same attributes, such as components and their variant counts.
Numeric columns, aligned to the end so digits line up.
whenNotToUse: Page layout: use the layout grids.
Two or three facts about one record: use a list.
Merged cells: rowspan and colspan are not supported.

properties.name: State
properties.note: Table. Focus is the ring on the focusable wrapper.

properties.name: Align
properties.note: Table Header Cell and Table Cell. Right is for numeric columns.

all.padding: Spacing/space-3 vertical, Spacing/space-4 horizontal (cells and caption)

Default.note: wrapper Background/Default/Default, Border/Default/Default at Stroke/thin; header cell Background/Default/Secondary; caption Text/Default/Secondary

Focus.note: Default plus the focus ring: Stroke/focus, Stroke/focus-gap, Border/Utilities/Focus Ring, Radius/radius-lg

accessibility.note: The wrapper is a focusable region named by the caption (role region, aria-labelledby, tabindex 0), so keyboard users can scroll a wide table.
accessibility.meaning: Header cells use scope col and row headers scope row; rowspan and colspan are not supported. Interactive elements inside cells need their own unique accessible names.

classRoles..data-table: Wrapper: border, radius, background, horizontal scroll and the focus ring.
classRoles..data-table__caption--hidden: Visually hidden caption that stays in the accessibility tree.
classRoles..data-table__head-cell--end: End-aligned header cell, for numeric columns.
classRoles..data-table__cell--end: End-aligned data cell, for numeric columns.

contract: Wrapper: a div with role region, aria-labelledby pointing at the caption id, and tabindex 0. The wrapper is always focusable so keyboard users can scroll it; there is no script that toggles it.
Inside the wrapper: a table with a caption (first child), thead, and tbody.
Header cells are th with scope col. Row headers are th with scope row. Data cells are td. No rowspan or colspan.
A numeric column puts the end modifier on its header cell and on every cell of that column.
Do not hide the caption with display or visibility. Use the hidden caption modifier instead.
Interactive elements inside cells need their own unique accessible names.

components.name: Alert
components.summary: Persistent inline message in four types: Info, Success, Warning and Error. Optional title, action and dismiss. Fluid width (Figma shows 480).
whenToUse: A message that stays with the content it is about, such as a form-level result or a notice on a page.
Error and Warning when the user needs to act or must not miss it.
whenNotToUse: A passing confirmation that disappears by itself: use Toast.
A brand strip, not a status: use Banner.

properties.name: Description
properties.default: Description of the message goes here.

all.gap: Spacing/space-3 between icon, content and dismiss; Spacing/space-1 inside the content

accessibility.note: Error uses role="alert", Warning, Info and Success use role="status".
accessibility.meaning: The dismiss button needs an accessible name, and the type never relies on color alone: the glyph and the text say it too. Live-region roles (alert, status) announce content that is inserted into the page. An Alert already present when the page loads needs no role to be read: apply the role when you inject the message. MDN: developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/alert_role and .../status_role.

knownGaps.text: The dismiss button is 16 by 16 as in Figma, under the 24 by 24 minimum of WCAG 2.5.8. A transparent ::after grows the hit area to 24 by 24 (4px on every side) without changing the layout. The action is far from the dismiss in the Alert, so the areas do not overlap.
Figma defines no hover, no underline and no focus for the action. The CSS uses the Hope focus ring and no hover change.

Role by type (owner decision, 2026-11-23): Error uses role="alert", Warning, Info and Success use role="status". MDN: role=alert is for information that needs immediate attention, role=status for advisory information that is not important enough to be an alert; it assigns neither Warning nor Success to a role. The W3C pages were not read verbatim.

The 1px border against the page background (1.4.11, 3:1): Info 7.54:1 Light and 2.26:1 Dark, Success 3.25 and 5.25, Warning 2.63 and 6.49, Error 5.87 and 6.88. Failures: Info in Dark (2.26) and Warning in Light (2.63); Success against its own fill is 2.86 in Light. The type is also carried by the glyph, the fill and the text, and the status icon passes 3:1 in every type (4.78 to 9.52).

components.name: Toast
components.summary: Floating, passing feedback in four types: Success, Warning, Error and Info (a neutral message uses Info). Message, optional description, action and dismiss. The positioning region and the timing are not part of this component.
whenToUse: Short feedback after an action, such as "Saved" or "Message sent".
whenNotToUse: A message that must stay until read: use Alert.

accessibility.note: Error uses role="alert", Warning, Info and Success use role="status".
accessibility.meaning: The dismiss button needs an accessible name, and the type never relies on color alone: the glyph and the text say it too. Live-region roles (alert, status) announce content that is inserted into the page. An Alert already present when the page loads needs no role to be read: apply the role when you inject the message. MDN: developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/alert_role and .../status_role.

knownGaps.text: The container that positions and stacks toasts is not coded.
Auto-dismiss timing, and pausing it on hover or focus, need JavaScript and are not coded.
Figma defines no enter or exit motion.
Figma uses the notification layer 500. The CSS uses --z-notification (500), part of the z-index scale added in v2.11.0.

The Toast border (Border/Default/Default) is 1.29:1 on the page background in Light and 1.28:1 in Dark, under the 3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11. The shadow (Shadow/lg) does not count as a boundary for that criterion. The text and icons pass.

The dismiss button is 16 by 16 as in Figma. A transparent ::after grows the hit area to 24 by 24 (WCAG 2.5.8). The action sits about 12px from the dismiss, so the grown area (4px beyond the button) does not overlap the action.

components.summary: Short text hint on a dark bubble with an arrow, in four placements: Top, Bottom, Left and Right. The bubble and the arrow are one piece; the CSS draws the piece, not the positioning against its trigger.

A hint that repeats something the page already says: the tooltip is never the only place for essential information.
whenNotToUse: A link, a button or long content: use a Popover.
Anything a touch user needs: a tooltip does not appear on touch.

accessibility.meaning: The text is a hint, not the only name of the control: an icon-only control keeps its own accessible name (aria-label). A tooltip does not appear on touch, so it never holds the only way to reach essential information.

components.name: Progress
components.summary: Determinate progress: an 8px track with a fill, an optional label and an optional value. Figma shows five values (0, 25, 50, 75, 100); in code the fill is any percentage.
whenToUse: An operation whose progress is known, such as an upload or a step count.
whenNotToUse: A wait with no known percentage: use Spinner.

all.height: 37 with the label and the value
all.gap: Spacing/space-2 between the label row and the track

accessibility.note: A div with role="progressbar", aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuenow, named by the label (aria-labelledby) or by aria-label.
accessibility.meaning: The visible value is hidden from assistive technology because the progressbar already reports it. The five Figma values have modifier classes (.progress__bar--0 to --100). Any other percentage is set with the --progress-value custom property on the bar, and the author keeps aria-valuenow in sync with it: CSS cannot read the ARIA attribute.

knownGaps.text: The native <progress> matched the geometry in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, but Firefox draws the fill (::-moz-progress-bar) without honoring transitions: the fill jumped, while Chromium and WebKit animated. The component is therefore a div with role="progressbar". Decision for the owner to confirm.
Figma has no indeterminate Progress. For a wait with no known percentage use Spinner.
Figma defines no fill motion. The fill animates its width with the base duration and ease-in-out; the global reduced-motion rule removes it.
The block measures 36.8 with the 13px label at line-height 1.6 and the 8px track plus Spacing/space-2; Figma shows 37.

components.name: Spinner
components.summary: A 24 by 24 ring with an arc of about 99 degrees that turns once per second in a linear rotation, for a wait with no known duration. One size.
whenToUse: A short wait with no known percentage, such as loading a list.
whenNotToUse: A wait with a known percentage: use Progress.
The loading shape of content: use Skeleton.

accessibility.note: A container with role="status" and visually hidden text, written by the author in the language of the page; the ring is aria-hidden.
accessibility.meaning: The spinner only says that something is busy. It has no value, so it is not an indeterminate progressbar. Under prefers-reduced-motion the rotation becomes an opacity pulse.

example.markup: Loading

knownGaps.text: The rotation is linear, one turn per second (Figma Core, decided in v2.12.0). With ease-in-out over a full turn the arc nearly stopped at 12 o'clock once per turn, so the curve was changed. ease-in-out stays only on the pulses: the Spinner reduced-motion pulse and the Skeleton pulse.

Under prefers-reduced-motion the ring pulses its opacity between 1 and 0.3 over 1.6s instead of turning. Figma does not name the replacement; the CSS overrides the global reduced-motion rule for this one animation, with !important, because a stopped spinner would look frozen.

The ring track is 1.29:1 on the page in Light and 1.28:1 in Dark. The track is a guide: the arc carries the state and the busy state is announced through role=status. The arc passes (19.42 and 17.06).

components.name: Skeleton
components.summary: A placeholder that imitates the shape of content while it loads: Text (12 high), Title (20), Avatar (40 circle) and Block (120). The width is fluid; Figma shows 240 for Text and Block and 160 for Title.
whenToUse: A load of the page layout that takes more than about 300ms, so the page does not jump when the content arrives.
whenNotToUse: A load shorter than that: show nothing.
A single control waiting for a result: use Spinner.

accessibility.note: The container carries aria-busy="true" and the pieces are aria-hidden.
accessibility.meaning: The pieces are decorative. aria-busy tells assistive technology the region is still loading; when the real content arrives, remove it. The pulse stops under prefers-reduced-motion.

knownGaps.text: Figma describes a soft pulse in ease-in-out but gives no duration. The CSS uses two periods of --duration-deliberate for a full cycle (opacity 1 to 0.5 and back). This is a reading of the data; the owner confirms or gives the value.
Figma shows fixed widths (240, 160). The CSS is fluid: the width belongs to the layout, set on the piece or its container.

The fill is 1.29:1 on the page in Light and 1.28:1 in Dark. The pieces are decorative placeholders; whether 1.4.11 applies to them is contested in the literature and there is no normative text, so it stays a documented gap.

components.name: Icon Button
components.summary: A 44 by 44 round button with one 24px icon, in Primary and Ghost, with Default, Hover, Focus and Disabled. It has no visible text, so it needs an accessible name.
whenToUse: A compact action whose icon is well known, such as add or close.
Primary for the one main action of a group, Ghost for secondary actions.
whenNotToUse: An action that needs a visible label: use Button.
The dismiss of an Alert or Toast: they have their own 16px control.

contrastNonText.case: Primary Hover icon on its fill
Disabled Primary icon on its fill (exempt, inactive)
Disabled Ghost icon on the page (exempt, inactive)

accessibility.focus: An outline of 2px (--focus-ring-width) with a 2px offset (--focus-ring-gap) follows the pill, giving the 52 by 52 ring of Figma.
accessibility.naming: Icon Button has no visible text: every instance needs an accessible name (aria-label), as the Figma description states.
accessibility.disabled: Disabled uses the native disabled attribute and the disabled tokens, not opacity. A disabled button leaves the tab order.
accessibility.note: A native button: Tab reaches it, Enter and Space activate it. The icon is aria-hidden and the name comes from aria-label.
accessibility.meaning: The icon is decorative. The accessible name says what the button does ("Add item"), never the name of the icon.

components.name: Menu
components.summary: A panel of actions or options opened from a trigger: 36px items, optional groups separated by a divider, a danger tone for destructive actions and a check on the chosen option.
whenToUse: A short list of actions on an object, opened from a button.
The options of a Select (the same panel look).
Put destructive actions last, after a divider.
whenNotToUse: Free content, a form or rich layout: use a Popover.
Page navigation: use links or Tabs.

whenToUse: A short decision that must be taken before the person goes on: confirm, cancel, choose.
Keep it short and about a single decision (the Figma text).
A destructive confirmation uses the destructive Button as the main action.
whenNotToUse: Extra context tied to an element, or a small control: use a Popover, which does not block the page.
A list of actions on an object: use a Menu.
A long form or a flow with several steps: use a page.
Zooming an image: use a Lightbox.

The shared ring (2px, 2px gap) following the pill radius (Figma Info text).

The Lote 4 report measured about 96 for Cancel because the demo label was "Cancelar" (8 letters) and Figma uses "Cancel" (6): a measurement artefact, not a CSS difference. The 0.2 to 0.8 px difference is the Plus Jakarta Sans text width and the 44.8 height (13px at 160%) against 45.

Resolved in v2.13.1. The Figma Info text defines the X: it follows the Icon Button Ghost behavior. Hover fills Background/Default/Secondary (--color-bg-alt) and the X goes to Icon/Color Default; Focus is the ring of 2px with a 2px gap; the icon color is --icon-color-secondary; the accessible name stays. The hover fill is a 28 by 28 circle, which also covers the corner tips of the X. Since D-44 the Figma component description and Info state the same 28px circle, so it is no longer only a choice of the code. It is not a new component.

Approved rule (Figma Info text, 2026-11-24), replacing the 24px margin of v2.13.0: the width is min(480px, 100% - 32px) (16px each side, --space-4), the height is limited to 100dvh minus the same margin, the body scrolls (overflow auto) and the header and the footer stay in view. A bottom sheet for touch would be a separate component, not created yet. Tested at 320, 390 and 768 wide, with a long body, and at 200% zoom.
Figma defines no motion, so the Modal opens and closes without animation. There is nothing to remove under prefers-reduced-motion.

The Modal uses the same approach as the Lightbox (the hidden attribute, a script for the focus trap, Escape, inert and scroll lock), not the native <dialog> element. Moving to <dialog> is an open decision: the top layer ignores z-index, so the Toast (500) would stay under an open Modal unless the Toast also moves to the top layer.

While a Modal is open the rest of the page is inert. A .toast and any element with data-modal-keep stay active so a notification still reaches the person. The Toast layer (500) is above the Modal (200).

Content that can hold text, links or a small control (the Figma text says free content).

contrastNonText.case: Close X (white at 80%) on the scrim (needs 3:1)

accessibility.targetSize: 36 by 36: above WCAG 2.5.8 (24 by 24) and under 2.5.5 (44 by 44, AAA).
accessibility.focus: The close button takes a 2px ring with a 2px offset in Border/Accent/Default (Solar, --color-border-accent-default), 44 by 44 around the 36 circle: the Light focus color (Anchor) is only 2.22:1 against this scrim, while Solar is 9.02:1 in Light and 12.08:1 in Dark.
accessibility.note: role="dialog" with aria-modal="true". The focus moves to the close button on open, stays inside, and returns to the image on close. Escape, the close button and a click on the backdrop close it. The page behind is inert.
accessibility.meaning: The close button is identified by the X (10.2:1 and 13.04:1), so its low-contrast glass fill and edge do not carry information. The X is white in both themes on purpose (dark mode era item: reevaluate when dark mode lands). The image keeps its own alt text.

classRoles..is-zoomable: Added by js/lightbox.js to an image that opens the viewer.
classRoles..lightbox: The overlay shell, layer 200. Built by js/lightbox.js.
classRoles..lightbox__panel: Image and caption, up to 960 wide.
classRoles..lightbox__media: Hugs the image, so the close button sits at the corner of the image.

knownGaps.text: Decided in Figma (Lightbox close, 2026-11-24): the X uses the primitive white in BOTH themes and does not follow Icon/Color, because the Lightbox scrim is dark in both. Icon/Color Neutral would turn ink in Dark. Intentional; a dark mode era item: reevaluate when dark mode lands.

The Figma effect is a raw background blur of radius 12 (not a style, no token). The CSS uses blur(6px): the Figma radius is double the CSS radius, so Figma 12 renders as CSS blur(6px), and Figma's own code export gives blur(6px). The source of this equivalence is Figma forum answers on blur in Dev Mode, not the official docs. Accepted divergence in docs/data/accepted-divergences.json (decided by Renan, 2026-11-24). No blur token matches, so the value is a literal: open item.
Known accepted divergence D-05: the Dark value of Scrim Strong is #000000e0 in Figma and #0d0d0fe0 in the CSS (the same value in both themes). Not changed in this release.

The image height is limited to the viewport minus the overlay padding, the 40px of the close button on each side and room for a caption of three lines, so the close button always stays inside the viewport. Figma does not define narrow screens.
Figma has one image and no previous or next controls. They are not built.
The close fill is 1.46:1 and the stroke 1.79:1 against the scrim in Light (1.37 and 1.69 in Dark). The X, which identifies the button, is 10.2:1 and 13.04:1. The ring is 9.02:1 and 12.08:1.

components.name: Avatar
components.summary: A circle with the initials of a person in three sizes (32, 40 and 56), or their photo.
whenToUse: Identify a person next to their name or on their own.
Three sizes: Small (32), Medium (40) and Large (56).
For a photo, fill the circle with the image and do not render the initials (the Figma text).
whenNotToUse: An icon or a logo: use an icon or an image.
A status or a count: use a Badge.
anatomy: Circle: --radius-pill, fill Border/Default/Default.
Initials: Small Body/SemiBold/body-xs, Medium Body/SemiBold/body-sm, Large Heading/H3. They are content, not generated.
Photo: the image fills the circle (object-fit: cover) and the initials are not rendered.
states: An image fills the circle and the initials are not rendered.
keyboard: None
An Avatar is not interactive. If it is clickable, wrap it in a link or a button that has its own name.
aria: Initials with the name next to them: aria-hidden="true", the name is already read.
Initials without the name next to them: role="img" and aria-label with the name (one announcement of the name instead of the letters).
Photo with the name next to it: alt="" (decorative).
Photo without the name next to it: alt is the name of the person.

accessibility.targetSize: Not interactive. 32, 40 and 56 are all above 24 by 24.
accessibility.note: The initials version is decorative when the name is next to it (aria-hidden); otherwise it is role="img" with an aria-label, which is announced once as the name. A photo has alt="" when the name is next to it, and the name as alt when it is not.
accessibility.meaning: The Avatar never carries information alone: the name is always available, next to it or as its accessible name.

example.markup: RM RM RM LL Luiza Laus

classRoles..avatar: The circle, Small by default: fill, initials and the pill radius.
classRoles..avatar__image: A photo that fills the circle.

knownGaps.text: The site has its own avatar rules: the testimonial card (40 by 40, same size and fill as Medium), the about page (56 with a 1.5px border, which Figma does not have) and the hero (115, outside the scale). They are unchanged; the site markup was not touched.
In Figma a photo is an image fill on the circle with the initials hidden. In code it is an inside the circle.
The circle (Border/Default/Default) is 1.29:1 on the page in Light and 1.28:1 in Dark. The initials, which carry the information, are 15.05:1 and 13.28:1. The name is always available as text.

components.name: Tag
components.summary: A pill of 28px that can be removed: a label and an optional X. The whole Tag is the button. It is not a Badge, which is static and shows a status.
whenToUse: A removable value, such as an applied filter or a chosen option.
The whole Tag is the button; the X is a visual cue inside it.
If the Tag is not interactive, use a Badge (the Figma text).
whenNotToUse: A status or a count that does not change: use a Badge.
A navigation link: use a Link.

all.width: 12 + content + 12 + 2 of border (67 for the label "Tag" with the dismiss icon)
all.focusRing: 75 by 36 around a 67 by 28 tag (4px outside each side), pill

anatomy: Pill: 28 high, radius pill, 1px border, padding 0 12, gap 4.
Label: Body/Medium/body-sm medium, Text/Default/Default.
Dismiss (optional): X 14px in the Icon/Color Secondary mode, a visual cue and not a second button.
states: Ring 2px with 2px gap around the whole Tag, following the pill.
Fill, border, text and icon from the Disabled tokens, no opacity. Uses the disabled attribute.
keyboard: Enter and Space
Remove the Tag (the whole Tag is the button).
Delete and Backspace
Remove the Tag when it has the focus (the Figma text).
Tab
Moves between Tags. After one is removed, the focus goes to the next Tag, else the previous one, else the parent.
aria: The Tag is a <button type="button">; the X is aria-hidden.
The accessible name is the visible label plus the action, for example aria-label="Remove filter Design".
js/tag.js fires a cancelable "hope:tag-remove" event before removing it, so the application can update its state.
Disabled uses the disabled attribute.

contrastNonText.case: Dismiss icon (Icon/Color Secondary) on the fill (needs 3:1)

accessibility.targetSize: 28 high: above WCAG 2.5.8 (24 by 24) and under 2.5.5 (44 by 44, AAA). Tags are separated by space in a list.
accessibility.focus: An outline of 2px with a 2px offset around the whole Tag, 75 by 36 around a 67 by 28 tag, following the pill (radius 18 in Figma).
accessibility.note: A <button> whose accessible name is the label plus the action ("Remove filter Design"). Delete or Backspace removes it when it has the focus; a click does the same. Disabled uses the disabled attribute.
accessibility.meaning: The X is a cue inside the button, not a second control. A Tag that is not interactive is a Badge.

classRoles..tag: The pill (a button): 28 high, border, fill and the label style.

knownGaps.text: The Tag border (Border/Default/Default) is 1.29:1 against the page in Light and 1.28:1 in Dark, and 1.21:1 and 1.14:1 against the Tag fill; the fill is 1.07:1 and 1.12:1 against the page. All are under the 3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11. Implemented exactly as in Figma, no color changed. The Tag is the first to reevaluate (together with the Alert and Toast borders); a possible swap is Border/Utilities/Input (--color-border-input, 3.12:1 on white).
knownGaps.reevaluate: first in the list: when dark mode lands, or with real use

knownGaps.text: A Tag without the dismiss icon is still a button. A Tag that is not interactive is a Badge (the Figma text), so there is no non-interactive Tag.
The Disabled fill and border are the same color (Background/Disabled/Default and Border/Disabled/Default), as in Figma, so the Disabled Tag shows no separate edge.

In the Figma Focus variant the border is drawn with the default stroke and the ring is a separate 75 by 36 frame. In code the ring is the outline of the button (offset 2, width 2), the same 4px outside each side.

components.name: Accordion
components.summary: A stack of items whose header opens and closes a panel of content. Each item has a title, a chevron and a bottom border; an open item shows its content.
whenToUse: Content in short sections that the person opens only when needed, such as answers to common questions.
The list is composed of stacked items (the Figma text).
Items open independently.
whenNotToUse: Content that has to be read in full: show it on the page.
Switching between views of the same object: use Tabs.
A list of actions: use a Menu.

properties.name: Content
properties.default: Content revealed when the item is open. Keep it scannable and relevant to the title.

item.width: fills the container (480 in the specimen)
item.border: bottom only, 1px Border/Default/Default, included in layout (closed item 54 = 16 + 21 + 16 + 1)
item.header: title and chevron 20 at the right, gap Spacing/space-3
item.focusRing: 488 by 62 closed and 488 by 112 open around the whole item, square

Closed.focus: Default plus a ring around the whole item

default.text: Content: Text/Default/Secondary, Body/Regular/body-sm; chevron rotated 180 degrees

Open.focus: Default plus a ring around the whole item

anatomy: Item: padding 16, gap 8, only a bottom border of 1px. The last item keeps its border.
Header: a button with the title (Body/SemiBold/body-sm semibold) and a CaretDown of 20px at the right, 12 apart.
Panel: the content (Body/Regular/body-sm, Text/Default/Secondary), hidden when closed.
states: The panel has the hidden attribute, aria-expanded="false", the chevron points down.
The panel shows, aria-expanded="true", the chevron is rotated 180 degrees.
The whole item takes Background/Default/Secondary, open or closed.
A ring around the WHOLE item (4px outside each side), square, though the focus is on the header button.
Title and chevron in the Disabled tokens, no opacity. Uses the disabled attribute.
keyboard: Enter and Space
On the header: open or close the panel.
Tab and Shift+Tab
Move between the headers (and into the content of an open item).
aria: The header is a <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the panel. It sits inside a heading; the level is the author's.

The panel has role="region" and aria-labelledby (the header) only when the list has 6 items or fewer; with more, both are omitted so the landmark list is not flooded. js/accordion.js applies the rule.
A closed panel uses the hidden attribute, so it is out of the accessibility tree.
Disabled uses the disabled attribute.

accessibility.targetSize: The click target is the full item width and at least 54 high (the padding is part of the target): above 2.5.5 (44 by 44, AAA).
accessibility.focus: An outline of 2px with a 2px offset around the whole item, square: 488 by 62 closed and 488 by 112 open for a 480 wide item. Where :has() is not supported, a plain ring on the header button is used, so the focus is never invisible. The container must not set overflow, or the ring would be clipped.
accessibility.note: The header is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls; Enter and Space toggle it. The panel is role="region" with aria-labelledby only when there are 6 items or fewer. A closed panel is hidden with the hidden attribute.
accessibility.meaning: The state is carried by aria-expanded and by the chevron direction, not by color. The border is a separator and carries no information.

classRoles..accordion__item: One item: padding 16, bottom border 1px, hover fill, focus ring on the whole item.
classRoles..accordion__heading: The heading around the header button (the level is the author's).

knownGaps.text: Figma draws Disabled only for the closed item (7 variants). An open and disabled item is not designed; in code a disabled item should be closed.
Figma defines no height animation, so the panel appears and disappears at once and the chevron turns without a transition. There is nothing to remove under prefers-reduced-motion.

The bottom border (Border/Default/Default) is 1.29:1 against the page in Light and 1.28:1 in Dark, and 1.21:1 and 1.14:1 against the hover fill, under the 3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11. It separates items and the title carries the information. Implemented as in Figma, no color changed.
knownGaps.reevaluate: when dark mode lands, or with real use

knownGaps.text: The ring on the whole item uses :has(.accordion__trigger:focus-visible). Where :has() is not supported, a plain ring on the header button is used instead. The focused item is raised one layer (--z-raised) so the ring is not painted under the next item.

Without JavaScript the items stay closed (the panels have the hidden attribute) and their content is not readable. Accepted: showing the content by default was considered and rejected, because an open Accordion on first load can push other elements out of view and looks wrong. The role="region" rule by item count is applied by the script.
The site has no accordion or FAQ pattern, so no page was aligned. design-system.html uses <details> for code blocks, which is a different pattern and was not changed.
